title: Slice sites of a simplicial object and their augmentation
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] whose underlying category has all fibre products, and let $U_\bullet:\Delta^{op}\to\mathcal C$ be a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Give $\mathcal C/U_n$ the localized topology: a family over $U_n$ covers exactly when its underlying family in $\mathcal C$ covers [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For a simplicial operator $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, the base-change functor $\mathcal C/U_p\to\mathcal C/U_q$, $W\mapsto W\times_{U_p}U_q$, is continuous and defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C/U_q\to\mathcal C/U_p$. These morphisms form a simplicial diagram of sites through the canonical isomorphisms of iterated fibre products, with their identity and cocycle laws. Its total site has objects $(n,V\to U_n)$ and morphisms $(q,V\to U_q)\to(p,W\to U_p)$ given by an order-preserving $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ and a morphism $f:V\to W$ with $w f=u_\alpha v$. Coverings are the families within one degree whose underlying families in $\mathcal C$ cover. This is the same site as the total site obtained from the slice-site diagram using base-change functors: the arrow $f$ corresponds to $V\to W\times_{U_p}U_q$. If $a:U_\bullet\to X$ is an augmentation with $X\in\mathcal C$, it induces a geometric morphism $b:\mathrm{Sh}((\mathcal C/U_\bullet)_{total})\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Its component morphisms $b_n$ are the localization morphisms induced by $a_n:U_n\to X$. Each $b_n$ is also the morphism of sites $\mathcal C/U_n\to\mathcal C/X$ given by the continuous base-change functor $\mathcal C/X\to\mathcal C/U_n$, $W\mapsto W\times_XU_n$; the two give the same geometric morphism, with $(b_{n,*}F)(W\to X)=F(W\times_XU_n\to U_n)$. Moreover $(b^{-1}E)_n=b_n^{-1}E$, where $(b_n^{-1}E)(V\to U_n)=E(V\to U_n\to X)$; the transitions are induced by the canonical composition identifications.

source.place: Tag 09WL, lemma-sr-when-fibre-products, clauses (1)-(3); the slice-total category and topology of section-hypercovering. Augmentation component inverse image is the construction in Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site. The identification of each localization morphism with the morphism of sites given by base change is Sites, Tag 09W9 (lemma-relocalize-given-fibre-products), as cited in the proof of 09WL.

proof.text: For each $u_\alpha:U_q\to U_p$, the base-change/localization node gives a continuous functor $\mathcal C/U_p\to\mathcal C/U_q$. Fibre products in a slice are computed by the corresponding fibre products in $\mathcal C$, so the canonical associators for iterated base changes preserve pullbacks of covering families. With $I=\Delta^{op}$ and $u_\alpha:\mathcal C/U_p\to\mathcal C/U_q$ contravariant in the displayed sense, the corrected coherent-total-site node applies; its unitors, compositors, and generated vertical-cover topology supply the identity and composition comparisons and their coherence for the slice diagram.

source.place: Tag 09WL proof of (1), using Sites 09W9; coherence and pullback stability are the general total-site construction of Tag 09WC

proof.text: Applying the total-site node to these slice sites gives objects $(n,V\to U_n)$ and arrows represented by $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$ and $V\to W\times_{U_p}U_q$ over $U_q$. By the universal property of the fibre product, such a map is equivalent to a map $f:V\to W$ satisfying $wf=u_\alpha v$, exactly the arrow description in the statement. Since the total topology is generated by vertical families, its coverings are precisely the families in one degree whose underlying families cover in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 09WL proof of (2), together with Tag 09WF and the fibre-product universal property

proof.text: For an augmentation $a:U_\bullet\to X$, composition with $a_n:U_n\to X$ gives the component localization morphism $b_n$. For $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$, the augmentation identity $a_p\circ u_\alpha=a_q$ gives a canonical identification of functors $\mathcal C/X\to\mathcal C/U_q$: first base change to $U_p$ and then along $u_\alpha$ is canonically $(W\times_XU_p)\times_{U_p}U_q\cong W\times_XU_q$. The base-change/localization node identifies each $b_n$ with this continuous functor and its induced geometric morphism. These identifications satisfy the unit and composition cocycles by the fibre-product associator, so the component inverse images form the coherent augmented diagram required by the systems and augmentation nodes; the systems equivalence itself allows arbitrary transition maps. Those nodes therefore give the geometric morphism $b$ from the total topos to $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/X)$ and its equalizer direct image.

source.place: Tags 09WL (3) and 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site; Sites 09W9 for each component

proof.text: The component formulas are obtained by evaluating the localization/base-change adjunction: $(b_{n,*}F_n)(W\to X)=F_n(W\times_XU_n\to U_n)$, while the localized-site definition gives $(b_n^{-1}E)(V\to U_n)=E(V\to U_n\to X)$ because restriction to $U_n$ is sectionwise $E(V)$. The augmentation node supplies the canonical transition maps and says that the direct image of the total sheaf is the equalizer of the two degree-zero-to-degree-one maps, so these component evaluations do not assert a separate value for $b_*F$.

The identity and cocycle laws for the component adjunctions and for the transitions are inherited from the coherence isomorphisms in the total-site and augmentation nodes. The construction uses only smallness, fibre products, and the stated localized covering topology; no properness, surjectivity, or hypercover hypothesis is introduced.
